applies_why: The judge labels the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row UNDERDETERMINED by treating its competing readings as balanced, which is the kind of single-verse openness K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C1 (Acts 2:30): UNDERDETERMINED -- [CR2] and [CR3] answered the loins/seed row with Genesis 46:26 and Hebrews 7:10 (loins at depth) and the legal/flesh distinction, while [DR3] presses that the only named Davidic man is Joseph; neither chain forces the other.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: I interpreted 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand': the judge could mean only a chain-level stalemate (allowed) or could be treating the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row's competing senses as open (forbidden); the text's focus on that row and its two readings supports the latter.
why: Because the judge makes the competing readings of the Acts 2:30 loins/seed row the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, it treats the verse as open instead of letting both senses stand as K-S2 requires.
